components.title: The Water Cycle
components.subtitle: How water moves between the oceans, the air, the land, and living things

components.text: The sun heats water in oceans, lakes, and rivers. The heat turns liquid water into water vapour, a gas that rises into the air.
As water vapour rises, it cools and condenses onto tiny particles of dust and salt. These droplets gather together to form clouds.
When droplets in a cloud grow heavy enough, they fall as rain, snow, sleet, or hail. The water then runs off into rivers or soaks into the ground, eventually returning to the oceans.

components.label: WORKED EXAMPLE
components.title: Tracing one raindrop
components.body:
A puddle on a sunny road evaporates. The vapour rises, cools high in the sky, and condenses onto a dust particle to form a cloud droplet.

The droplet joins others until it is heavy enough to fall as rain. It lands on a hillside, soaks in, and eventually seeps into a stream that flows to the sea.
components.takeaway: One drop of water can pass through every stage of the cycle.

questions.question: What is the main energy source that drives evaporation?
questions.explanation: The sun's heat turns liquid water into vapour.

questions.question: Which process forms clouds from water vapour?
questions.explanation: Condensation happens when vapour cools and gathers into droplets.

questions.question: What is the name for water that soaks into the ground?
questions.explanation: Infiltration is when water seeps into soil and rock.
